Sciurus.distinguishing_notes: Sciurus vs Tamiasciurus (N. America): Tamiasciurus smaller (key: total length <360 mm, tail <140 mm vs >360/>140 in S. carolinensis/S. niger; anterior border of orbit opposite last premolar vs opposite M1 - Chapman et al. 2007 key); Tamiasciurus has 3 transbullar septa (Moore 1959) and 2n=46 (HMW) vs 2 (Sciurus s.str.) and 2n=40/42; summer black lateral line typical of Tamiasciurus but also present in S. aberti. Sciurus vs Microsciurus/Sciurillus (Neotropics): larger (HB >=140 vs Sciurillus 89-115; Microsciurus 108-160 overlaps S. pucheranii/S. ignitus at 140-160); ears project above the crown (Emmons & Feer via Mammalian Species accounts); upper incisors not procumbent in all Sciurus examined vs procumbent in Microsciurus and Sciurillus (Voss et al. 2024); Sciurus skull retains frontoparietal suture and has a masseteric tubercle, unlike Sciurillus (Moore 1959; Voss et al. 2024). Number of upper premolars and mammae are homoplastic and do NOT separate Sciurus from Microsciurus (de Abreu-Jr et al. 2020). Sciurus vs Syntheosciurus: no clean external character found; Moore 1959 separates by cranial details (Syntheosciurus: interparietal sutures fused, upper incisors proodont, P3 present, P4 as large as M3) but these also partly occur in Sciurus. Sciurus vs flying-squirrel genera: patagium (absent). Sciurus vs chipmunks/ground squirrels: see dorsal stripes (Sciurus has at most a single mid-dorsal band) and low-crowned cheek teeth.

Microsciurus.distinguishing_notes: Microsciurus vs Sciurus: small (HB 108-160 mm; Sciurus >=140), small ears generally not reaching above crown (conflicting statement in Sciurillus MS account), procumbent upper incisors, 6 mammae, 2 upper premolars (Voss et al. 2024) - but premolar and mammae counts overlap with several Sciurus species (de Abreu-Jr et al. 2020), and Microsciurus as traditionally defined is polyphyletic. Size overlaps S. pucheranii and S. ignitus (140-160 mm). Microsciurus vs Syntheosciurus: interparietal sutures remain distinct in adult Microsciurus but are completely fused in Syntheosciurus (Moore 1959); Syntheosciurus larger (HB 150-185). Microsciurus vs Sciurillus: Sciurillus smaller (HB 89-115 vs 108-160, overlap 108-115 only via M. alfari), pale gray vs brown/olivaceous (Mammalian Species accounts), skull of Sciurillus lacks masseteric tubercle and visible frontoparietal suture and has jugal-frontal contact (Moore 1959; Voss et al. 2024).

Sciurillus.distinguishing_notes: Sciurillus pusillus vs Sciurus and Microsciurus (Amazonia/Guianas): smallest Neotropical squirrel, HB 89-115 mm (Sciurus >=140; Microsciurus 108-160, i.e. overlap only with the smallest M. alfari, which is not sympatric - M. flaviventer 120-160); pale gray grizzled pelage with underparts not contrasting (MS account: only pale gray squirrel in the Amazon; Microsciurus brown); short ears not extending beyond crown (vs long ears in sympatric Sciurus). Cranially unique (Moore 1959; Voss et al. 2024): no masseteric tubercle, no visible frontoparietal suture in adults, jugal-frontal contact, single transbullar septum, infraorbital canal at least as long as maxillary toothrow. Two upper premolars and six mammae, like Microsciurus. Baculum axe-shaped (HMW).

caveats: Taxonomy follows MDD v2.5 (context file), which keeps a broad Sciurus (29 spp.) and Microsciurus (10 spp.); many sources use other arrangements (de Abreu-Jr et al. 2020 genera Guerlinguetus, Hadrosciurus, Leptosciurus, Echinosciurus, etc.; HMW 2016 with 4 Microsciurus spp. and broad M. flaviventer/M. mimulus). Species coverage was mapped through MDD synonymy notes (e.g., gilvigularis in S. aestuans; sanborni in S. ignitus; mearnsi in T. douglasii; otinus/sabanillae/similis/simonsi formerly M. flaviventer; boquetensis/isthmius formerly M. mimulus). HMW text comes from Plazi OCR and contains artifacts (e.g. "262-3" = 262.3; "pro6dont" = proodont); quotes are verbatim from that text. HMW S. oculatus head-body (508-560 mm) is evidently total length and was discarded. Tamiasciurus hb_length_mm is a derived conservative superset (no observed HB range found for T. hudsonicus or T. douglasii). Patagium "absent" for all five genera rests partly on inference (gliding squirrels = Pteromyini per Jackson & Thorington 2012) plus explicit key couplets for S. niger, S. carolinensis and T. hudsonicus. Characters with scope "partial" are documented only for the listed species and should be treated as unknown for the genus if the key requires full coverage. The Microsciurus "ears project above crown" character has conflicting sources. Cheek pouches, snout elongation and upper-incisor grooves are essentially undocumented for this group (no source found stating them), although they are generally not reported in tree squirrels. Quotes were verified programmatically as exact substrings (whitespace-normalised) of the retrieved texts.
